name: comp-252

frames.best_why: Knob is pulled well past the middle with the readout at 55, showing the full track and both speaker icons.

tagline: A speaker slider that raises a number as its knob slides right.
summary: A sound-level setting inside a dark card. A muted speaker, a horizontal level slider and a loud speaker sit on one row, with the current level printed beside the heading.
appearance: A bordered dark card holds a small heading with a grey helper line, then a row with the word Volume on the left and a number on the right. Beneath it a muted speaker icon, a grey track with a round white knob, and a speaker icon at the far end.
behaviour: Sliding the knob right lengthens the white filled portion and raises the number beside Volume. The knob gains a soft ring while it is being dragged and everything settles in place on release.
demo_content: Card title "Sound" with the line "Adjust the output level for notifications and media.", a Volume row starting at 25.
search_phrases: sound level control for a media app
slider with small and large speaker icons
number next to a volume knob
speaker icon on each end of a track
use_when: A settings panel or player needs a readable sound level with the current number in view.
avoid_when: The two speaker icons are decoration only, so there is no working mute toggle here.
customise: The Volume label and the starting level are written in the source; the icons and number layout need edits to change.
weight_why: A card, one track and a couple of icons; nothing runs until the knob is dragged.

a11y.note: The slider is labelled for screen readers, but the speaker icons are hidden from assistive tech and the number is not tied to the slider.

polish_why: Well spaced card with a clear hierarchy; the control itself is a stock slider.
title: Volume Slider
